The receipt confirms only that rosbridge accepted the publication, not motion, arrival or stopping. /cmd_vel is also a physical TurtleBot3 command topic, so this action is R2.

facts.text: The turtlebot3_fake_node package is a ROS 2 ament_cmake package that depends on rclcpp.
The package description says the node supports simple tests without a robot.
The constructor names the node turtlebot3_fake_node.

The constructor creates an odom publisher, a joint_states publisher and a tf publisher on relative names, then one cmd_vel subscription, then a 10 ms wall timer; it creates no ROS service or action server.
The odom publisher is nav_msgs::msg::Odometry.
The joint_states publisher is sensor_msgs::msg::JointState.
The cmd_vel subscription is geometry_msgs::msg::Twist on the relative name cmd_vel.
The wall timer is created with a 10 ms period and calls update_callback.

command_velocity_callback records the command time, copies cmd_vel.linear.x and cmd_vel.angular.z to goal velocities and computes the two wheel-speed setpoints from the wheel separation; it returns void and publishes no acknowledgement.
init_variables sets cmd_vel_timeout_ to 1.0 s.
update_callback's stale-command watchdog zeroes both wheel-speed setpoints when the last cmd_vel sample is older than cmd_vel_timeout_; its comment reads 'stop the robot if no cmd_vel'.
update_callback publishes odometry, joint states and tf on every timer tick.
update_odometry comments label the translational velocity [m/s] and the rotational velocity [rad/s].
init_variables names the two wheel joints wheel_left_joint and wheel_right_joint and sizes position, velocity and effort to two entries.
update_joint_state copies last_position_ into position and last_velocity_ into velocity for the left and right wheels.

update_odometry sets each wheel's last_velocity_ to its wheel-speed setpoint divided by wheel_radius_ and adds that rate times the step time to last_position_; its comment labels the wheel rotation value [rad].
The constructor assigns a KeepLast(10) QoS and passes that QoS to the odom publisher.
update_callback assigns odom_.header.stamp from time_now and publishes odom_.
update_odometry assigns odom_.pose.pose.position.x and y from odom_pose_ and sets z to 0.
update_odometry builds a quaternion with setRPY of odom_pose_[2] and assigns it to odom_.pose.pose.orientation.
update_odometry adds delta_s and delta_theta, computed from wheel_l and wheel_r, to odom_pose_.
init_parameters reads wheels.separation into wheel_seperation_ and wheels.radius into wheel_radius_, and the default of each get_parameter_or call is 0.0.
The burger parameter file sets wheels.separation to 0.160 and wheels.radius to 0.033.
The fake-node launch includes rviz2.launch.py and starts the turtlebot3_fake_node and robot_state_publisher executables.
turtlebot3_drive creates a geometry_msgs::msg::Twist publisher on the relative name cmd_vel.
turtlebot3_drive's update_cmd_vel assigns linear.x and angular.z and publishes that Twist.

determinism.notes: Event-driven canned responses; the /odom burst is a placeholder unicycle stepped by the subscription throttle, not the node's 10 ms integrator or a physics step

gaps: the fake is a ROS-free canned transport: it answers the declared /cmd_vel, /odom and /joint_states endpoints and runs no turtlebot3_fake_node code, physics or 10 ms timer

odometry and wheel values are placeholders; a non-zero /cmd_vel is recorded and is not stored, and a burst while that command holds is a projection the next read does not keep; a zero Twist freezes the stored pose. This is not the node's trajectory or its 10 ms timing

the confirmation subscribes to /odom with throttle_ms 50 so five counted samples span (5-1)*50 ms = 200 ms (min_span_ms). The node publishes every 10 ms (turtlebot3_fake_node.cpp:59); an unthrottled window of five samples spans 40 ms and cannot meet min_span_ms. The fake spaces producer stamps by the subscription throttle_rate; a live rosbridge throttle_rate is not run here

the pose span thresholds are operator_required (the clone states no at-rest bound). fixtures/estop-confirmation.json holds fake placeholders only. A live simulation sets its own in simulation_deployment['estop_confirmation']; client bounds may only tighten the window

init_parameters defaults wheels.separation and wheels.radius to 0.0 (turtlebot3_fake_node.cpp:88-89). cpp:194 divides each wheel speed by wheel_radius_. cpp:204-210 replace a NaN wheel increment with 0. cpp:215 multiplies by wheel_radius_. cpp:216 multiplies by wheel_radius_ and divides by wheel_seperation_. Both defaults still 0 and a zero command make delta_theta NaN, and the pose becomes non-finite. Radius 0 with a non-zero separation and a zero command keeps delta_s and delta_theta at 0, so the pose stays finite while the wheel velocities stay NaN. A non-zero command with radius 0 makes delta_s non-finite. The pose-only confirmation does not read joint velocities and does not validate wheel geometry: a finite stationary pose still confirms. burger.yaml sets separation 0.160 and radius 0.033 (burger.yaml:3-5). Those yaml numbers are not limits

the fake-node launch starts turtlebot3_fake_node and robot_state_publisher and includes rviz (launch.py:60-75) and does not publish /cmd_vel. turtlebot3_drive in this clone creates a Twist publisher on cmd_vel and publishes linear.x and angular.z (turtlebot3_drive.cpp:42, 98-104); CMakeLists.txt builds that executable and no launch file in the clone starts it. A competing /cmd_vel publisher (that node, a teleop node or Nav2) keeps the pose moving and the confirmation fails closed
the 1 s stale-command watchdog (cpp:157-161) is a second path. The confirmation does not read it and does not rely on it. The fake has no wall-clock timer and does not reproduce it

/cmd_vel is also the command topic of a physical TurtleBot3. A rosbridge endpoint pointed at that robot would move it. This package declares only the fake node, in simulated mode, and claims nothing beyond the confirmation window

the package does not expose /tf, the Gazebo worlds, /scan, /imu, the camera or any ROS service or action. There is no unpause and no re-enable: reset re-confirms the /odom pose read-only and resumes nothing
every number in fake.py is a placeholder, including the initial 0.2 m/s command, the 12-sample burst, the 0.033 m radius and 0.160 m separation used only to fill joint velocities, and the stamp clock

confirmation.description: zero velocity commanded on /cmd_vel and the fake node's /odom pose (position x and y, orientation z and w) still within the operator's bounds in five consecutive fresh stamped samples within the confirmation bound
predicate: max - min of odom.pose.pose.position.x over the window <= rest_x
max - min of odom.pose.pose.position.y over the window <= rest_y
max - min of odom.pose.pose.orientation.z over the window <= rest_qz
max - min of odom.pose.pose.orientation.w over the window <= rest_qw

safe_state.description: Simulated only: zero velocity commanded on /cmd_vel and the fake node's /odom pose (position x and y, orientation z and w) still within the operator's bounds in five consecutive fresh stamped samples within the confirmation bound. The zero-Twist publication alone proves nothing; another /cmd_vel publisher can move the base again; nothing is claimed beyond the confirmation window.
